title: Reduce voice-call talk-latency (Israel/Render)
summary:
Aggressive latency reduction for the relay-based voice call app, driven by user reports of mid-call talk-delay while hosting on Render's free tier.

Changes:
1. Server transport (server/server.js): set socket.setNoDelay(true) on every upgraded WebSocket connection to disable Nagle (was adding up to ~40 ms of coalescing delay per hop), and disable perMessageDeflate so tiny PCM frames skip zlib.
2. Frame batching (src/main.js): accumulate a few encrypted frames into one WebSocket binary message (FRAME_BATCH=2, ~21 ms) with a short flush timer; receiver splits the fixed 1052-byte frames and decrypts each. Cuts per-message overhead and delivery jitter. E2E encryption (per-frame nonces) preserved.
3. DTLN denoiser moved off the main thread into a Web Worker (new src/denoiser-worker.js); src/audio.js forwards raw frames to it and applies the noise gate on return. Keeps the DTLN denoiser fully (user requirement); falls back to main-thread denoiser when Worker is unavailable or errors, so no regression.
4. Playback jitter buffer (src/player-worklet.js): lowered initial priming target 640->384 (~13->8 ms) and FLOOR 320->256 (~6.7->5.3 ms); adaptive growth retained.
5. Deployment guidance (server/README.md, src/main.js comment): recommend deploying the relay in the region closest to callers — Frankfurt for Israel/Europe, not the default Oregon — and keeping a free Render instance awake via a /healthz uptime ping to avoid cold-start latency.

Validation: full vitest suite (310 tests) passes; added tests for batched split/decrypt round-trip and worker fallback.
userVisibleChange: Lower talk-latency in voice calls: frames no longer delayed by Nagle/compression, audio batched into fewer WebSocket messages, DTLN denoiser runs off the main thread, and the playback buffer starts smaller. Biggest real-world win is redeploying the Render relay in Frankfurt (closest region to Israel) instead of Oregon.

risks.title: Module Worker support in Tauri WebView
risks.mitigation: Falls back to main-thread denoiser if `new Worker(... {type:'module'})` throws; verified fallback test. Tauri v2 WebView2 is Chromium-based and supports module workers.

risks.title: Fixed 1052-byte frame assumption in batching
risks.mitigation: Capture path always emits fixed 512-sample (1024-byte) frames, so the encrypted wire size is deterministic; receiver splits by fixed size safely.

decisions.title: Region over code for the biggest win
decisions.rationale: Every audio frame makes two WebSocket hops through the relay, so the relay's region dominates talk-delay. For Israel, Frankfurt is far closer than Oregon; this is a config/deploy change, not code.

decisions.title: Keep the relay architecture
decisions.rationale: True peer-to-peer (WebRTC+TURN) would remove the relay hop but contradicts the project's explicit 'no NAT traversal' design; out of scope. Batching + transport tuning is the in-code path.

decisions.title: Worker denoiser with main-thread fallback
decisions.rationale: User insisted the DTLN denoiser stay. Moving it to a module Web Worker removes main-thread jitter without removing the feature; fallback preserves behavior where Workers are unavailable (e.g. jsdom tests).
